Note::TexAccessor::ids¶

Back to Note TeX Accessor API Reference

Signature¶

TokenBatch Note::TexAccessor::ids() const

Extract ASCII Identifier Lexemes¶

ids() returns identifier-shaped lexemes found inside complete math regions. An identifier begins with an ASCII letter and may continue with ASCII letters, digits, or underscores. Thus x, x_1, and argmax_x are each one token. Numbers cannot begin an identifier.

This is intentionally lexical rather than semantic. In \sin(\alpha), both sin and alpha are identifier lexemes because the backslash is not part of the identifier pattern. Choose math_funcs() or greek() when category membership matters, and symbols() when the leading backslash must survive. No symbol table, declaration lookup, or expression parser is involved.

Prose outside math and incomplete or escaped math regions are ignored. Tokens retain repetitions and source order, and offsets map the flattened result back to every input cell. Undefined input propagates; non-text dtypes are rejected.

Example 1: Variables And Command Bodies¶

const auto source = pluss::make_note(
    std::vector<std::string>{
        R"(prose 99; $x_1 + \sin(\alpha) = 2.5$)",
        R"(\[\beta \leq y^2\] and \(\sqrt{z}\))",
        R"(escaped \$7 and plain theta)",
        R"($$\argmax_x f(x) \approx 10$$)"},
    std::array<std::int64_t, 2>{2, 2});
const auto result = source.tex().ids();
std::cout << result.tokens() << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[12], dim=1, numel=12, encoding=utf8)
["x_1", "sin", "alpha", "beta", "leq", "y", "sqrt", "z", "argmax_x", "f", "x", "approx"]

There is no token for prose theta or the exponent 2. Command bodies such as leq and approx do appear because this method is deliberately lexical.

Example 2: Read A Single Cell’s Range¶

const auto offsets = result.offsets().integers();
for (std::int64_t i = offsets[1]; i < offsets[2]; ++i)
  std::cout << result.tokens().at(i) << '\n';

Output¶

beta
leq
y
sqrt
z

Example 3: Undefined And Invalid Dtypes¶

std::cout << std::boolalpha
          << pluss::Note::undefined().tex().ids().tokens().defined() << '\n';
try {
  (void)pluss::note::make(std::vector<std::int64_t>{1}).tex().ids();
} catch (const pluss::Error&) { std::cout << "identifiers Int64: rejected\n"; }

Output¶

false
identifiers Int64: rejected

See Also¶

  • nums: extract unsigned decimal-number lexemes.

  • math_funcs: classify recognized function commands.

  • greek: classify recognized Greek-letter commands.
